1	# Team performance evaluation
2	
3	English | [中文](team-performance.zh.md)
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	The Team performance suite measures the costs that a human or Member can observe across loading, tool calls, ledger reads, Session work, and collaboration. It is an evaluation tool, not a production code path, and it runs only when explicitly enabled.
8	
9	The source of the scenarios is [`scripts/team-performance/`](../../scripts/team-performance/). The script index lists the entry points and their output formats in [`scripts/README.md`](../../scripts/README.md).
10	
11	## Run the evaluation
12	
13	### Baseline
14	
15	Run the default 16 scenarios in one Node process:
16	
17	```sh
18	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team
19	```
20	
21	The command writes a run directory under `artifacts/team-perf/runs/` containing `manifest.json`, measured `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json`. The default configuration uses three measured samples and one warmup. Use `DSH_BENCH_SCENARIOS` to select scenarios and the matching variables such as `DSH_BENCH_THREADS`, `DSH_BENCH_FOLLOWERS`, `DSH_BENCH_MEMBERS`, and `DSH_BENCH_SESSION_EVENTS` to change workload size.
22	
23	### Scale matrix
24	
25	Run the default 15 cases in separate Node processes:
26	
27	```sh
28	npm run bench:team:matrix
29	```
30	
31	Set `DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_CASES` to a comma-separated list of `scenario:threads:followers`. The matrix routes the first size to Member or Session workloads when the scenario requires it. Each matrix directory contains a manifest, each child run, and an aggregated `results.json`.
32	
33	### Browser loading
34	
35	Measure the assembled Web bundle and Team mode:
36	
37	```sh
38	DSH_BENCH_BROWSER_SAMPLES=3 npm run bench:team:browser
39	```
40	
41	Each sample uses a fresh temporary Web scaffold and Chromium. The runner records page load, Workspace connection, ordinary ready, Team mode ready, navigation timing, transfer bytes, console warnings, and page errors. It writes `manifest.json`, `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json` under `artifacts/team-perf/browser/runs/`. Browser results must be read with p95 and p99 and with the individual samples because cold startup variance is material.
42	
43	### Semantic probes
44	
45	Check the ordered post-commit notification queue:
46	
47	```sh
48	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics
49	```
50	
51	The probe checks failed delivery retry, per-Member ordering, Client invalidation before notification drain, shutdown cancellation, and disposal errors. A passing timing run does not replace these checks.
52	
53	### Compare runs
54	
55	Compare two baseline summaries or two matrix result files:
56	
57	```sh
58	npm run bench:team:compare -- before/summary.json after/summary.json
59	npm run bench:team:compare -- --max-regression 20 before/summary.json after/summary.json
60	```
61	
62	The comparator reports shared p50, p95, and p99 rows and separately reports missing scenarios and metrics. A regression threshold is meaningful only when the workload, environment, and scenario schema match.
63	
64	## What the scenarios measure
65	
66	| Area | Scenarios | Main evidence |
67	| --- | --- | --- |
68	| Loading and activation | `bundle-size`, `host-boot`, `member-activation`, `member-activation-batch`, `member-resume` | bundle bytes, Host fixture boot, new and resumed Member activation, sequential versus concurrent activation |
69	| Tool paths | `tool-call`, `tool-read-sweep`, `thread-read-reply`, `tool-write`, `notification-retry` | tool total, Host handler time, result bytes, read/reply and failed-delivery recovery |
70	| Collaboration | `collaboration-fanout`, `collaboration-agent-turn` | durable commit, Ledger queue wait/service, fan-out dispatch, event-loop lag, notification drain, model request and idle stages |
71	| Session and storage | `session-fold`, `session-replay-jsonl`, `ledger-read-memory`, `ledger-replay-sqlite` | cursor and projection fold, JSONL write/read/bytes, bounded ledger reads, SQLite open/replay/validation |
72	
73	The baseline uses real Team Host fixtures and deterministic model adapters where a model turn is needed. It does not claim to represent a production model provider or a live user's machine. The browser scenario is the assembled-path check; the Node scenarios explain the cost inside that path.
74	
75	## Current constraints
76	
77	- Notification read material is reused only during one delivery attempt. Facts, delivery plans, and projections are not long-lived caches or a second authority.
78	- A commit affecting at least eight Members queues notification effects after the durable commit and Client invalidation. Effects remain ordered per Member and are scheduled independently across Members. Effects that have not started when shutdown begins are skipped; the next activation derives the durable unread facts again.
79	- JSONL `zstd` remains the production default. Uncompressed replay is faster in the measured fixture but uses substantially more disk space.
80	- Concurrent calls already improve the measured batch Member activation path. The result alone does not justify changing Host startup ordering without a separate startup-restoration experiment.
81	- Browser cold-start results have a long tail. Keep the sample records and compare distributions; do not turn one run into a hard acceptance threshold.
82	
83	## Change workflow
84	
85	When changing a performance-sensitive path, run the narrowest scenario that can observe the change, then run the related scale cases and semantic probes. Compare the same scenario before and after the change. Inspect operation counts and result shape together with wall-clock values; a lower time with missing facts is a failed run. Run `npm test` and `npm run check:artifact` before treating the result as delivered.
86	
87	Do not place secrets, real profiles, or temporary browser overlays in the repository. The benchmark is opt-in, so ordinary development and release checks do not run it.

# Team 性能优化迭代

## 问题

Team 的性能成本分布在启动、模型 tool call 和成员协作三条链路。当前缺少一套能把用户或模型等待时间拆成 queue、ledger、通知 fan-out、Session/Agent 和 Client 阶段的统一基线，因此局部优化无法证明端到端收益。

已有实验确认：通知路径会重复派生 Thread/Main unread 和 delivery plan，并随未读 Thread 数增长；纯读 tool 的并行分类在当前同步 projection 读取上只有很小且不稳定的收益。

## 目标

- 以“动作发起到结果可继续使用”的端到端 p95 为主指标。
- 同时记录 queue、ledger、post-commit fan-out、Session/Agent 和 Client 阶段。
- 保留原始 JSONL 样本、环境信息和规模输入，结果可在固定版本上复跑。
- 在不改变 ledger 单一权威、记录级校验、通知语义和公开协作契约的前提下，降低重复派生。

## 选择的方案

第一阶段按三条垂直切片推进：

1. 建立 Team 专用 baseline runner 和默认关闭的结构化观测。
2. 把一次通知投递所需的 Thread/Main unread、delivery plan 和文本输入收敛成一次性只读派生结果，由 Host 在同一次投递中复用。
3. 用真实 Host、SQLite、Member fixture 和规模阶梯验证优化前后 p50/p95，并记录失败、冷唤醒和多 Member 场景。

Host queue、fan-out 和协作因果使用默认关闭的结构化 hook；tool/render 阶段优先用测试 wrapper。通知 read set 只在单次投递内存在，不建立长期缓存或第二个 durable authority。

## 关键决定

- 主指标是端到端 p95；单个函数耗时只能作为定位信息。
- Thread 消息到成员回复是主协作场景；DM、Task claim 和 cold wake 作为补充场景。
- `team_inbox`、`team_thread read`、所有写入和所有 wake 副作用继续独占。
- 当前不为纯读 tool 增加 `isConcurrencySafe`。实验显示同步 projection CPU 工作无法通过 Harness parallel pool 加速，p95 收益不稳定。
- 跨 commit debounce、长期 read-set 缓存、通知上限调整、Member 激活并行和 Session fold 增量不进入首个实现切片。
- 旧版 Attention source 的升级重放与新格式稳态分别测量，不把用户未提交工作树混入 clean baseline。

## 验收 seam

- 启动：storage open、ledger replay/validate、Session inventory、Member activation、Host ready。
- Tool call：模型 call、参数处理、Host handler、queue wait、ledger/query、结果 render 和 Session 写入。
- 协作：A commit ack、B notice queued、B notice claimed、B read、B reply committed、B idle。
- 通知 read set：旧路径与新路径的 notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt、steer/followup 次序和失败隔离逐项一致。
- 规模：1/20/100 unread Thread、1/8/32 follower、SQLite 与内存 fixture、warm/cold Member。

## 开放问题

- Session fold 增量是否仍是长 Session 的主要成本，需要独立真实日志基线。
- Member activation 是否能安全并行，需要生命周期资源和失败边界实验。
- 当 Team 读取引入真实异步 I/O 后，是否重新评估纯读 tool parallel。

# scratch-review

Review a change through the work item that explains why it exists. Check the implementation against its spec, correctness, repository standards, and unnecessary complexity; leave a report that a later session can act on.

Do not modify implementation code, ticket status, or the work-item continuation README. A review produces evidence, not fixes.

## 1. Resolve the target

Accept a work-item directory or one of its `issues/NN-<slug>.md` files, optionally with `--base <ref>`:

```text
/scratch-review .scratch/active/<work>
/scratch-review .scratch/active/<work>/issues/02-<slug>.md --base main
```

Read the target's `README.md`, `DESIGN.md`, and selected ticket. For a work-item review, read all in-scope tickets and their status. Use their acceptance criteria as the spec; use the design for intent and boundaries. Do not infer a spec from a branch name. If the selected scope has neither a ticket nor explicit acceptance criteria, report the spec gap instead of inventing requirements.

If the repository has no `.scratch` work area, or the user supplied only a diff or ref, perform a normal code review in the conversation. Do not initialize `.scratch` or manufacture a work item just to store a report.

## 2. Pin the code range

The review must name the exact code it examined.

- With `--base <ref>`, verify the ref, use `git diff <ref>...HEAD`, and record `git log <ref>..HEAD --oneline`. Also inspect uncommitted changes and untracked files separately.
- Without `--base`, review the working tree, including untracked files. If it is clean, ask which fixed point to compare against; do not silently choose a branch or commit.
- For a single ticket, use the tickets, commit list, and design to exclude unrelated changes. Record anything that could not be separated.
- Read the complete relevant diff and enough surrounding source to verify behavior. An empty or unresolvable range means an incomplete review, not a pass.

## 3. Review three axes

Run these as independent read-only sub-agent reviews in parallel when the harness supports it; otherwise perform them sequentially. Give each reviewer the exact range, relevant spec, and source locations. Aggregate and verify their candidates rather than pasting their reports together.

### Spec

For every acceptance criterion, determine whether it is implemented, partial, missing, or not verifiable here. Report behavior outside the requested scope and requirements that appear implemented but behave incorrectly. Cite the ticket or design passage supporting each finding.

### Correctness

Trace concrete inputs and states through the changed code. Look for behavioral regressions, boundary and error-handling mistakes, security problems, and missing tests for important behavior. Report a failure scenario, not a vague concern. Run relevant existing checks to confirm or reject candidates.

### Standards and simplicity

Read the repository's documented standards that apply to the change. Cite the rule behind a standards finding; the repository overrides general style preferences. Skip what tooling already enforces.

Also look for code that can be removed without losing required behavior: hand-written standard-library functionality, unnecessary dependencies, unused flexibility, speculative abstractions, and avoidable duplication. State what replaces it, including "nothing" for dead code. Do not treat line count as a quality metric or suggest removing meaningful tests.

## 4. Verify

Run the repository's relevant existing tests and checks against real inputs where practical. Add targeted edge cases when needed, without modifying the implementation. Never claim a check passed without running it. Distinguish observed behavior from code inspection, and human-only acceptance from automated verification.

A failed check is not automatically a defect in this change: establish whether it predates the range before attributing it. Record unrelated failures as limitations.

## 5. Save the report

From this skill directory, allocate the report with:

```bash
python3 scripts/start_review.py <work-item-or-ticket>
```

The script resolves a ticket to its work item and creates a new empty report under `reviews/`, numbered monotonically: `01-<scope>.md`, then `02-<scope>-recheck.md`, and so on. It refuses targets outside a `.scratch` work item and never overwrites an existing report.

Fill that new file using [assets/review-template.md](assets/review-template.md). Use the repository's documentation language. Write only this report; never rewrite an earlier review to make history look clean.

The conclusion is one of:

- **Pass** — no confirmed finding requires a change. This does not erase listed unverified scope or residual risk.
- **Changes needed** — at least one confirmed finding requires a change.
- **Incomplete** — the spec, code range, or evidence needed for a meaningful review was unavailable.

Order findings by severity. Each finding needs a location, concrete impact or failure scenario, supporting spec or standard where applicable, verification evidence, and the smallest appropriate fix. Do not create tickets, apply fixes, mark acceptance complete, or close the work item unless the user asks afterward.

In the conversation, give the conclusion, material findings, checks actually run, and a link to the saved report.

# .scratch Work Rules

This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.

## Work-item structure

Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.

```
active/<work>/
├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
│   └── 02-<slug>.md
├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
```

## Ticket discipline

Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):

```markdown
# NN — title

**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete

- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
```

- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).

## Lifecycle

- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.

## Version control

- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.

## Directory index

See [README.md](README.md).

# Team 性能优化迭代

## 问题

Team 的性能成本分布在启动、模型 tool call 和成员协作三条链路。当前缺少一套能把用户或模型等待时间拆成 queue、ledger、通知 fan-out、Session/Agent 和 Client 阶段的统一基线，因此局部优化无法证明端到端收益。

已有实验确认：通知路径会重复派生 Thread/Main unread 和 delivery plan，并随未读 Thread 数增长；纯读 tool 的并行分类在当前同步 projection 读取上只有很小且不稳定的收益。

## 目标

- 以“动作发起到结果可继续使用”的端到端 p95 为主指标。
- 同时记录 queue、ledger、post-commit fan-out、Session/Agent 和 Client 阶段。
- 保留原始 JSONL 样本、环境信息和规模输入，结果可在固定版本上复跑。
- 在不改变 ledger 单一权威、记录级校验、通知语义和公开协作契约的前提下，降低重复派生。

## 选择的方案

第一阶段按三条垂直切片推进：

1. 建立 Team 专用 baseline runner 和默认关闭的结构化观测。
2. 把一次通知投递所需的 Thread/Main unread、delivery plan 和文本输入收敛成一次性只读派生结果，由 Host 在同一次投递中复用。
3. 用真实 Host、SQLite、Member fixture 和规模阶梯验证优化前后 p50/p95，并记录失败、冷唤醒和多 Member 场景。

Host queue、fan-out 和协作因果使用默认关闭的结构化 hook；tool/render 阶段优先用测试 wrapper。通知 read set 只在单次投递内存在，不建立长期缓存或第二个 durable authority。

## 关键决定

- 主指标是端到端 p95；单个函数耗时只能作为定位信息。
- Thread 消息到成员回复是主协作场景；DM、Task claim 和 cold wake 作为补充场景。
- `team_inbox`、`team_thread read`、所有写入和所有 wake 副作用继续独占。
- 当前不为纯读 tool 增加 `isConcurrencySafe`。实验显示同步 projection CPU 工作无法通过 Harness parallel pool 加速，p95 收益不稳定。
- 跨 commit debounce、长期 read-set 缓存、通知上限调整、Member 激活并行和 Session fold 增量不进入首个实现切片。
- 旧版 Attention source 的升级重放与新格式稳态分别测量，不把用户未提交工作树混入 clean baseline。

## 验收 seam

- 启动：storage open、ledger replay/validate、Session inventory、Member activation、Host ready。
- Tool call：模型 call、参数处理、Host handler、queue wait、ledger/query、结果 render 和 Session 写入。
- 协作：A commit ack、B notice queued、B notice claimed、B read、B reply committed、B idle。
- 通知 read set：旧路径与新路径的 notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt、steer/followup 次序和失败隔离逐项一致。
- 规模：1/20/100 unread Thread、1/8/32 follower、SQLite 与内存 fixture、warm/cold Member。

## 开放问题

- Session fold 增量是否仍是长 Session 的主要成本，需要独立真实日志基线。
- Member activation 是否能安全并行，需要生命周期资源和失败边界实验。
- 当 Team 读取引入真实异步 I/O 后，是否重新评估纯读 tool parallel。

Is the new early return reachable in a state where the existing dedup would NOT have returned, and does it change behavior in a way that loses a delivery? Specifically: `covered` is `plan.delivered` from a previous attempt. Can `covered` be non-empty while the CURRENT facts differ (new unread facts arrived after the previous delivery)? # Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and Semantic Versioning. Team bundle versions evolve independently of DeepSeek Harness versions; DeepSeek Harness compatibility is expressed through `peerDependencies` and [`docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md`](docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md).

## [Unreleased]

**Upgrade note**

- Rules version 2 is now the default and the `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` preview switch is gone: this build adopts version 2 on every ledger it opens and no longer writes the version 1 kinds it replaced (`team/message-sent`; they replay inside version 1 segments only). A build at or below 0.2.5 refuses a ledger this build has opened, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` before opening the Team anywhere, and back up `agent_team.sqlite` first. Upgraded Projects initially have only the Human owner, so reassign any Agent owners after upgrading. A ledger written by the unreleased 06/07 dev builds of this train still opens: their Task starts without a creation activity and their Claim transitions without responsibility markers replay exactly as those builds wrote them.

**New**

- Tasks carry one accountable owner. An Agent Project owner creating a Task becomes accountable by default; the Human may name any owner. Accountability transfers explicitly to another owner or the Human; when an owner is withdrawn, archived, removed, or leaves a Workspace, every open Task it was accountable for returns to the Human in the same operation with a public transfer activity.
- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.
- Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
- A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
- `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
- The team-member persona separates naming from mentioning: a Member referred to in plain prose — Iris, Ferry — is a reference, while `@Handle` in a Message body is a delivery, so a stray `@` inside a roster explanation or a quoted report no longer interrupts Members who need not act on it.
- Notices are delivered by Attention. Every unread fact interrupts: a Main stream post, a new discussion, mentions, replies, ownership events, responsibility events and Task reminders wake immediately, and so does an ordinary Thread update for any Member following that Thread. The former owner and accountable threshold — five ordinary Thread updates per Member per Thread before a summary — is gone, so following a Thread now means being interrupted by its first ordinary update, and no identity places a reader in a slower class. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
- A Main stream commit wakes every Member whose Main stream Attention covers that stream, not only the Project's owners, so a non-owner follower is interrupted by the first ordinary update like anyone else. Following a Main stream requires Project membership, exactly as reading and writing it do, so an Attention row left behind by a departed Member delivers nothing and the follow cannot be the door that gets a Member in.
- An ownership grant no longer overwrites the Main stream Attention a Member already holds: a Member that followed and read before being granted ownership keeps its own read watermark, so granting ownership no longer silently clears its unread. The Human's own row is derived from owning the Project, so a Main stream unfollow from the Human is refused instead of committing an operation that changes nothing; `team_attention` takes `projectRef` or a Thread ref, never both, at the Host as well as the tool.
- A Thread the notice cannot render — the section cap or the character budget dropped it — keeps its facts undelivered, so the next relevant commit rederives and retries them instead of leaving them swallowed by a notice that never named them.
- An Attention row records what established it — starting the Thread, claiming its Task, being its accountable, owning the Project, being named in it, or choosing to follow — so a result can state why the reader follows instead of guessing. `team_attention` renders the cause once the reader follows, and a Claim result or a Thread start names the Attention it just established. The source is optional in storage: rows written before it existed keep their bytes; replay derives the missing cause from the operation that wrote the row and then validates the repaired projection strictly.
- The Main stream carries its own Attention, keyed by Member × Project and independent of any Thread's row, so ordinary Main stream unread no longer follows from owning the Project. The Human's row is derived from the Project's creation and only its read watermark is stored; an Agent's is written by the ownership grant, starting at the grant sequence so no historical backlog is inherited; any other Member's comes from an explicit follow. A Member that does not follow the Main stream holds markers alone — a mention or a reply still reaches it — and withdrawing ownership keeps the row, so the Member keeps its ordinary unread until it reads or unfollows. The Main stream standing's `owner` field is replaced by `following`.
- `team_attention` takes `projectRef` to follow or unfollow a Project's Main stream, mutually exclusive with `threadRef`/`taskRef`. Every Attention result states its consequence: following means ordinary updates from there interrupt you; unfollowing means they stop, while mentions, replies and responsibility events still reach you and no Claim or Task responsibility is released. `team_thread` states the reader's own Main stream Attention on a Main stream read, and prompts the unfollowed reader on a Thread read. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill no longer describe an owner threshold: no identity sits in a slower delivery class, owning a Project follows its Main stream rather than its Threads, and unfollowing stops ordinary updates only.
- Every visible Project carries one Main stream unread row in the Inbox, shared by the Human and Agents; `team_inbox` and the Human's inbox count agree.
- The task board: a `taskBoard` Host projection and Remote method lists every visible Project's open Tasks plus the last five finished per Project, and names the reader its `humanMemberId`. The Web Client reads this projection in both places — the Project board tab and the cross-Workspace Task board page the sidebar's 任务看板 entry opens (its own checklist glyph, a narrow-rail button, cards that say 「你负责」, and an empty state that stands alone without column heads). `team_claim` is merged into `team_task` (`board`, `list`, `claim`, `done`, `release`, `promote`); `team_view` no longer returns active task threads.
- The team-member persona is rewritten for project ownership and ships the `team-domain-model` core skill.
- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.

**Changed**

- Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original discussion context even after compaction with no unread. Already-visible Message bodies are explicitly omitted while the read acknowledges the same chronological batch; background, Main stream Thread cards, and current Task cards remain separate from newly acknowledged facts. Human reads and historical read receipts are unchanged.
- Agent `read` and `message` results share one output ceiling: the tool selects fewer facts, an oversized Message body returns in ordered parts, a read acknowledges only the prefix it can deliver and never crosses an incomplete Message, and repeating the same request resumes at the first missing segment of the current Session surface. A Thread read receipt records the selected bound, while receipts written before it keep the default batch; there is no offset parameter.
- Complete Thread Message rejections provide the facts and current token needed to reconsider a write without a mandatory extra read. The Host verifies exact Team source, Thread/Message identity, and the actual Session text; summaries and truncated results cannot satisfy the check. Partial rejections supply no token, and neither notifications nor rejections acknowledge unread work.
- Task and Claim Activities follow the same context rule as Messages. A notice, read/history result, or rejection binds the immutable event — actor, object, and recorded Claim refs or transfer endpoints — never current Task or Claim state; a complete mixed Message/Activity rejection supplies the Thread token, while partial facts do not. A Main stream post has no token and accepts complete pending entries from the current Session or an explicit read, and new unread entries, revision, permissions, and Task state are checked again.
- An Activity already fully visible in the current context is acknowledged by identity only, with its event marked as already present; the repeated identity does not bind a second time. An Activity is one line and cannot be split, so one beyond the output ceiling acknowledges nothing and reports that limit instead of offering continuation.
- Agent notices prioritize missing direct Messages and responsibility changes across Threads and the Main stream. Complete facts already in the current Session use short identities without repeating their bodies or creating another binding; replies retain their target. Scope and detail caps apply after ranking, and the whole notice including recovery instructions stays within one character budget. Omitted direct signals and Task reminders retain an explicit count and bounded reading routes. Main counts name their Project, and another Member's ownership change is counted without telling the reader they became an owner. Delivery, unread counts, and markers are unchanged.
- Member context updates identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and private memory separately. Editing `memory.md` produces a short stale-copy notice instead of repeating the full index and unrelated background; missing context restores the relevant current blocks. Empty ownership and reduced Workspace participation remain explicit.

The audit compares Team Client CSS/TSX against the design-language contract in `docs/frontend-design/principles-and-language.md`: focus visibility, control rhythm, icon semantics, hardcoded colors, and shipped-reference presence. Run it after any visible-UI change and after every DSH upgrade.

This builds first, copies built packages into a temporary profile, starts the official Harness Web scaffold, and runs the real journey with `/usr/bin/google-chrome` (override with `CHROME_PATH`). The sandbox setup provisions Playwright's own chromium at that path when the base image ships no browser. It cleans the temporary profile and Harness test files afterward.

There are three explicit preview/verification paths:

```sh
npm run preview:ui                         # keyless Team fixture
npm run test:browser                       # repeatable keyless browser acceptance
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... npm run preview       # real model interaction
```

`preview` and `preview:ui` use temporary profiles and storage and clean up on `Ctrl+C`. `preview` always uses the real DeepSeek adapter and fails when credentials are missing; it does not silently switch to replay. `preview:ui` uses a keyless route-only adapter whose fixture does not call a model; an accidental model request fails explicitly.

All three lanes stage this bundle and its declared dependency closure into a temporary profile, then name that staged copy as a profile package — the shape `dsh plugin add` leaves behind: a `file:` dependency, a link under the profile's own `node_modules`, and an entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The scaffold resolves plugin imports from a computed generation built out of `profile.layers`, so only a staged copy named there contributes the Team rows, and they come from the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.

A command-line overlay is not an equivalent mount. The Host row's Human-profile form is written to the profile document, and the config editor rejects that write while a later layer (a home patch or a command-line overlay) declares the same row — `overridden by a home patch or command-line overlay` — so the form stays unwritable. A staged bundle the scaffold never names resolves neither its own rows nor its dependency closure: every Team row reports `failed to import` with no module-resolution error to read, and the keyless fixture then fails on an `undefined` `ctx.agentTeam`.

`test:browser` does not cover the two preview lanes, so boot them by hand after any change to scaffold composition or profile resolution.

The browser journey uses a deterministic keyless Host/Client driver. It covers Agent Inbox reading/replying, Human Project and Thread navigation, persistence after reload, and restoration of the ordinary DSH surface after leaving Team mode.

60	  const delivered: (string | number)[][] = []

70	      delivered.push(reminderFacts)
71	    }

73	    if (now.length > 0) immediate.push([threadRef, ...now])
74	    // A Thread the notice cannot render is not delivered by this attempt, so its
75	    // facts are not what `covered` records: an unchanged rederivation still sees
76	    // them as owed and re-attempts instead of standing down.
77	    if (now.length > 0 && !undelivered.has(threadRef)) delivered.push([threadRef, ...now])

## Which operations wake a Member, and how recovery is chosen

A wake is one bounded coalesced notice the Host delivers over one of four causes, each carrying the durable fact that produced it:

| Cause | What produced it |
| --- | --- |
| `commit` | any committed operation touching the Member: a mention, a DM, a Task activity, a promotion, an accepted answer |
| `transition` | a recorded `team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-recycled`, or legacy `team/member-session-rolled-over` whose retire and activation effects complete out of order; the rederived Inbox is sequenced after any carried input |
| `activation` | a fresh activation, carrying the previous Session id when input was carried forward |
| `running` | the Member's own `agent/status` going `running` — one wake per transition, not per step |

Waking is not a second authority and never promises exactly-once model processing. A wake that fails delivery clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable facts and retries without a second append.

Base directory for this skill: /home/yu/.claude/plugins/cache/nowledge-community/nowledge-mem/0.7.26/skills/search-memory

# Search Memory

## When to Search

Run one targeted search before concluding continuation, review, regression,
release, connector, prior-decision, cross-tool, or exact-history work. References
to a previous fix, "that approach", or "like before" are strong signals.
The startup Context Bundle / Working Memory is a briefing, not a substitute
for this search. Do not wait for the user to explicitly request retrieval.

Skip trivial, independent tasks, generic syntax questions, and an explicit
fresh start.

## Search First, Then Read a Targeted Range

Before searching, briefly tell the user what prior context you are looking for.
Use the CLI; this plugin does not register an MCP server. If NMEM_CLI_PATH is
set, use its quoted value as the executable instead of bare nmem.

Start with the smallest relevant surface:

```bash
# Durable decisions, procedures, and learnings
nmem --json m search "3-7 core concepts" -n 5

# Prior conversations and exact discussion history
nmem --json t search "query" --limit 5
```

Keep the active Space from the Context Bundle. NMEM_SPACE selects an explicit
session-wide lane; legacy NMEM_SPACE_ID is compatibility-only. If an AI Identity
resolved another lane and no session override is set, pass that existing lane
with --space "<space name>". Never infer a Space from cwd, git, or a project name,
and never remove a selected lane because it returned no matches.

If normal memory search is weak or conceptual, try Deep Search once:

```bash
nmem --json m search "query" --mode deep -n 5
```

Inspect only relevant hits. Judge their content and server warnings rather than
applying one fixed score threshold across search modes. When a memory includes
source_thread, or thread search finds the likely conversation, inspect one small
targeted range for the specific messages needed:

```bash
nmem --json m get <memory_id>
nmem --json t show <thread_id> --limit 8 --offset 0 --content-limit 1200
```

Use a known target `--offset` once; do not advance through pages.
Use label, importance, or time filters only when they narrow this question. For code-backed knowledge,
verify the finding against the current repository before treating it as current.

## Respond Honestly

Use retrieved knowledge naturally and cite the memory or original thread when
it supports the answer. Distinguish a successful search with no relevant matches
from a CLI, authentication, timeout, or server failure. If retrieval is unavailable,
say so briefly and continue the authorized work.

A session-start receipt confirms briefing loading. A Bash search or Skill call
shows actual retrieval in the host transcript; do not claim a search occurred
because startup context was loaded.

## Troubleshooting

Run /nowledge-mem:status or nmem status to check the connection. If the CLI is
outside PATH, set NMEM_CLI_PATH to its executable path. Install nmem-cli with pip
or pipx if needed; Arch Linux users can use yay -S nmem-cli or paru -S nmem-cli.
For remote Mem, configure the shared client on this machine with
nmem config client set url and nmem config client set api-key.

### Bounded thread reads

Search memories or threads first, then choose the specific conversation and message range needed. Call `thread_fetch_messages`, a host thread-fetch tool, or `nmem --json t show` at most once per question, using a small message limit (for example 8) and a content limit of 1200 where supported. A known target range may use a nonzero offset once.

Never loop over offsets to reconstruct a conversation. Do not raise `--content-limit` to compensate for a slow or incomplete read. Small output limits do not guarantee cheap server-side work on every deployed backend. If a read is slow, incomplete, fails or times out, stop, report the evidence gap, and refine the search rather than retrying pages. A later explicit user request for another range is a new bounded read; a routine “continue” is not permission to drain the thread.

      "content": "[[dsh-agent-team]] 在 2026-10-28 做了一轮系统性的性能研究，最终把「性能问题」从直觉收敛到可测的结论：**真正的热点是通知 fan-out 的重复派生，而不是单次调用的 CPU 成本；并行化纯读 tool 是伪优化**。这套结论本身比任何单项数字更耐用，因为它给出了「先测什么、用什么指标判、什么条件下才该并行」的判据。

## 一、研究组织方式（先约束，再测量）
- 以 discussion 流程开一个 [[.scratch]] 工作项，耐用产出是 `materials/` 下的研究材料，后续收敛为 `DESIGN.md` 与 tracer-bullet tickets；过程材料不进生产代码。
- 实验纪律：只写工作项 `materials/` 与临时 artifacts，**不改生产代码**；基线必须在**干净 commit** 上跑，避免混入工作树红灯。
- 优先三项实验：通知重复派生的**调用次数**、纯读 tool 批次的串行/并行差异、启动与生成物的可重复基线。
- 只读审查范围：`c3a9704..HEAD` 与当前工作树，跟踪 Client 加载、Project/Board/UI slot、Remote 激活与 bundle 路径，不写文件、不跑会改动工作树的命令。

## 二、结构热点：通知 fan-out 的重复派生（已实测）
用真实 mountTeamMemberHost fixture，单次 fan-out 的**固定执行次数**为：`notificationFacts` 1、`mainNotificationFacts` 1、`inboxDeliveryPlan` 2、`notificationText` 1，`mainUnreadFrom` 派生 2 次；`unreadFor` 调用次数为 `N + min(N, 50) + 1`——100 个未读 Thread 时 151 次，而 Host **只渲染前 50 条通知，却扫描全部 100 个候选**。

规模表现：1/20/100 Thread 的 fan-out 核心中位耗时约 0.195 / 0.549 / 1.047 ms；通知派生占一次 reply 墙钟的比例从 **14.8% 升到 50.9%**，即用户感知延迟的主要来源随规模转移到通知侧。100 Thread 场景出现过一次 7.439 ms 长尾，样本量不足以计算 p95/p99。

只读审查给出的复杂度判据（解释为什么是结构问题）：
- 普通 Main 更新与新建讨论通知走 `emitCommitted → affectedMembersOf → notifyMember → notifyMemberAtWake → planInboxDelivery → followup/steer`，成本**至少 O(F)**（F = follower 数），且**每个 follower 重新派生一次完整 Inbox**，无批量合并、节流或并发上限。
- Main unread 改为按项目 Main source + marker 在 `mainUnreadFrom` 重算，`inboxForWorkspaces` 遍历候选 Thread 与 Main 项目，成本随项目数 P 与历史条目 E 增长，并被 fan-out 放大。
- 写侧 durable projection 在接收人数 R 下至少 O(R)；`planInboxDelivery` 每次建立 Set、遍历 unread facts 并对**完整序列集合 `JSON.stringify`**。
- cold wake 被 fan-out 放大（一次 Main post 可能同时激活多个 cold follower、重放 Session 并重建上下文），legacy replay 的修复检查仍为 O(N)。

## 三、优化顺序与已落地的最小一步
1. **先削重复派生，不谈并发**：第一阶段把 `deliverInboxNotice` 生成的 `InboxDeliveryPlan` 直接传给 `notificationText`，使每个受影响 Member 的 plan 由 2 次降为 **1 次**。
2. 完整的 `NotificationReadSet`（一次派生、全链路复用）尚未实施；`memberInbox` 与 `notificationFacts` 之间的 unread 派生重复、Main unread 重复**仍未解决**——这是后续的第一优先级。
3. 仍未测：SQLite backend（当前全部测量基于**内存 storage backend**）、多 Member 并发、持续增长的 Main backlog、多 cold member 同时 wake 的资源峰值、长 Main history 下 unread 扫描与 `JSON.stringify` 的增长曲线、legacy replay 在长 ledger 下的性能。

## 四、否定结论：纯读 tool 并行当前不值得
仅为性能给纯读 Team tool 加 `isConcurrencySafe` 的收益不足：
- 真实 AgentTeam Host 下 4/8 个调用并行，**p50 只缩短约 0.15–0.49 ms**，p95 不稳定（有一轮提升也有一轮变慢）；再一轮 4/8 并行 p50 也只有 0.2–0.5 ms。
- **同步 CPU 投影完全不加速**，只有能真正让出事件循环的异步等待才明显并行——而 Host 读路径当前是同步投影。
- 证据规模：三轮每格 51 样本的真实 Harness loop、两轮每格 101 样本的真实 AgentTeam Host、34 项 scheduler 与执行模式测试。
- 顺序安全性已验证：所有轮次的 tool call / tool result / 下一轮模型输入都保持模型顺序（串行写入为 call 与 result 连续成对，并行 async 为全部 call 后全部 result，sync 可能交错但各自仍保持模型顺序）——所以**不做并行不是正确性问题，是收益/复杂度问题**。
- 复测条件：若 Host 读路径转为真实异步，再重跑该实验。

## 五、可复用的两条测量纪律
1. **用确定性调用次数作结构热点的代理指标**，而不是墙钟 p95：小样本下 p95 算不出来，毫秒级收益淹没在噪声里；而 `unreadFor` 的调用公式 `N + min(N,50) + 1` 与固定派生次数是可复现、可对比的硬证据。
2. **测量环境必须写清边界**：内存 backend 上得到的增长曲线不能直接外推到 SQLite 与多 Member 并发场景，否则优化对象会被误判。

## 结论
一次性能研究的产出不应是「快了 X ms」，而是**排序过的热点清单 + 否定掉的伪优化**：通知 fan-out 的重复派生（plan 复用 → NotificationReadSet → 批量/节流）是真收益，纯读 tool 并行在当前同步 Host 上是假收益。

      "content": "[[dsh-agent-team]] 的 Team 性能优化在 2026-10-28/29 从「一次性研究」升级为「可持续的评测—改进闭环」。核心结论不是某个毫秒数，而是三样可复用的资产：一套能重复运行的评测矩阵、一批已落地的低风险派生复用、以及明确否定掉的伪优化与不可合入方案。

## 一、目标与组织（先约束，再测量）
- 长期目标由用户升级为：覆盖加载、tool call、协作流程的**可复用性能评测**（不限于现有场景），并基于评测持续自主改进；同时必须注意本地工作区可能存在的其他修改。
- 组织方式：以 discussion 流程开 [[.scratch]] 工作项，耐用产出进 `materials/`，最终收敛为 DESIGN.md 与 tracer-bullet tickets；过程材料不进生产代码。

- 只读审查：限定 `c3a9704..HEAD` 与当前工作树，跟踪 Client 加载、Project/Board/UI slot、Remote 激活与 bundle 路径，不写文件、不跑会改动工作树的命令。

## 二、评测矩阵（可复跑的入口，而非临时脚本）
入口集中在 `scripts/team-performance/`：
- `team-performance-baseline.ts`（默认关闭）：覆盖 bundle/Host、`team_view`、`team_inbox`+task+view+attention+thread read 的组合扫描、`team_message` post、`team_dm`、同步 fan-out、Agent cold/warm turn、内存 ledger 读取与 SQLite replay。
- `run-team-performance-matrix.mjs`：在**独立 Node 进程**中运行各规模 case，避免同进程 JIT/GC 串扰。
- `compare-team-performance.mjs`：比较 run summary 或 matrix results 在共同场景上的 p50/p95/p99，**显式报告缺失场景/指标**，`--max-regression` 可作回归门槛。
- `run-team-browser-performance.mjs`：Chromium 侧 loading 测量。
- `team-performance-semantics.ts`：通知失败重试、顺序保持、Client invalidation 与 shutdown 语义。
- 配套浏览器/UI 验证：`npm run test:browser`（冷启动与 Client 加载、Remote 激活、进入 Team 打开 Project 与 Board、创建 Task 后跳转、退出 Team 后普通 DSH 恢复）、`npm run preview:ui`、Chrome Performance 录制空数据与大数量 Board 首次渲染、「提交到卡片获得焦点」耗时、多个 Main follower 在线时一次 Main 更新造成的 Remote 请求数与刷新数；bundle 用隔离 worktree 双 commit 对比 `client.js` 原始/gzip/brotli 与 `npm pack --dry-run` 内容。

## 三、结构热点与已落地的收益
通知 fan-out 的重复派生是真热点，且用**确定性调用次数**度量：单次 fan-out 固定为 `notificationFacts` 1、`mainNotificationFacts` 1、`inboxDeliveryPlan` 2、`notificationText` 1，`mainUnreadFrom` 派生 2 次；`unreadFor` 为 `N + min(N, 50) + 1`（100 Thread → 151 次），而 Host 只渲染前 50 条通知却扫描全部候选。fan-out 核心中位耗时 1/20/100 Thread 约 0.195/0.549/1.047 ms，通知派生占一次 reply 墙钟比例从 14.8% 升到 50.9%。

已落地四项低风险派生复用：Thread unread facts、Main unread material、delivery plan（每个受影响 Member 由 2 次降为 1 次）、以及已有 coverage 的 running 重复读取。32 follower 样本中 `mainUnreadFrom` 由 66 次降到 33 次；优化后 `npm test` 129 个文件、1505 通过 1 跳过，语义测试与单 case matrix 复跑通过。**完整 NotificationReadSet 仍未实施**：`memberInbox` 与 `notificationFacts` 的 unread 派生重复、Main unread 重复仍是下一优先级。

## 四、两类否定结论（同样是资产）
1. **纯读 Team tool 并行是伪优化**：真实 Host 下 4/8 并行 p50 仅缩短约 0.2–0.5 ms，p95 不稳定；同步 CPU 投影完全不加速，只有能让出事件循环的异步等待才明显并行。顺序安全性已验证（tool call / result / 下一轮输入均保持模型顺序），所以不做并行不是正确性问题，是收益/复杂度问题。**复测条件**：Host 读路径转为真实异步后再跑。
2. **异步 fan-out 当前不能合入生产**：shutdown 后仍会执行排队的通知，语义不可接受；优化必须先保证语义门禁通过。

## 五、测量纪律（最耐用的部分）
- 用确定性调用次数与固定派生次数作结构热点的代理指标，而不是小样本 p95——毫秒级收益会淹没在噪声里。

1	# Team performance evaluation
2	
3	English | [中文](team-performance.zh.md)
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	The Team performance suite measures the costs that a human or Member can observe across loading, tool calls, ledger reads, Session work, and collaboration. It is an evaluation tool, not a production code path, and it runs only when explicitly enabled.
8	
9	The source of the scenarios is [`scripts/team-performance/`](../../scripts/team-performance/). The script index lists the entry points and their output formats in [`scripts/README.md`](../../scripts/README.md).
10	
11	## Run the evaluation
12	
13	### Baseline
14	
15	Run the default 16 scenarios in one Node process:
16	
17	```sh
18	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team
19	```
20	
21	The command writes a run directory under `artifacts/team-perf/runs/` containing `manifest.json`, measured `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json`. The default configuration uses three measured samples and one warmup. Use `DSH_BENCH_SCENARIOS` to select scenarios and the matching variables such as `DSH_BENCH_THREADS`, `DSH_BENCH_FOLLOWERS`, `DSH_BENCH_MEMBERS`, and `DSH_BENCH_SESSION_EVENTS` to change workload size.
22	
23	### Scale matrix
24	
25	Run the default 15 cases in separate Node processes:
26	
27	```sh
28	npm run bench:team:matrix
29	```
30	
31	Set `DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_CASES` to a comma-separated list of `scenario:threads:followers`. The matrix routes the first size to Member or Session workloads when the scenario requires it. Each matrix directory contains a manifest, each child run, and an aggregated `results.json`.
32	
33	### Browser loading
34	
35	Measure the assembled Web bundle and Team mode:
36	
37	```sh
38	DSH_BENCH_BROWSER_SAMPLES=3 npm run bench:team:browser
39	```
40	
41	Each sample uses a fresh temporary Web scaffold and Chromium. The runner records page load, Workspace connection, ordinary ready, Team mode ready, navigation timing, transfer bytes, console warnings, and page errors. It writes `manifest.json`, `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json` under `artifacts/team-perf/browser/runs/`. Browser results must be read with p95 and p99 and with the individual samples because cold startup variance is material.
42	
43	### Semantic probes
44	
45	Check the ordered post-commit notification queue:
46	
47	```sh
48	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics
49	```
50	
51	The probe checks failed delivery retry, per-Member ordering, Client invalidation before notification drain, shutdown cancellation, and disposal errors. A passing timing run does not replace these checks.
52	
53	### Compare runs
54	
55	Compare two baseline summaries or two matrix result files:
56	
57	```sh
58	npm run bench:team:compare -- before/summary.json after/summary.json
59	npm run bench:team:compare -- --max-regression 20 before/summary.json after/summary.json
60	```
61	
62	The comparator reports shared p50, p95, and p99 rows and separately reports missing scenarios and metrics. A regression threshold is meaningful only when the workload, environment, and scenario schema match.
63	
64	## What the scenarios measure
65	
66	| Area | Scenarios | Main evidence |
67	| --- | --- | --- |
68	| Loading and activation | `bundle-size`, `host-boot`, `member-activation`, `member-activation-batch`, `member-resume` | bundle bytes, Host fixture boot, new and resumed Member activation, sequential versus concurrent activation |
69	| Tool paths | `tool-call`, `tool-read-sweep`, `thread-read-reply`, `tool-write`, `notification-retry` | tool total, Host handler time, result bytes, read/reply and failed-delivery recovery |
70	| Collaboration | `collaboration-fanout`, `collaboration-agent-turn` | durable commit, Ledger queue wait/service, fan-out dispatch, event-loop lag, notification drain, model request and idle stages |
71	| Session and storage | `session-fold`, `session-replay-jsonl`, `ledger-read-memory`, `ledger-replay-sqlite` | cursor and projection fold, JSONL write/read/bytes, bounded ledger reads, SQLite open/replay/validation |
72	
73	The baseline uses real Team Host fixtures and deterministic model adapters where a model turn is needed. It does not claim to represent a production model provider or a live user's machine. The browser scenario is the assembled-path check; the Node scenarios explain the cost inside that path.
74	
75	## Current constraints
76	
77	- Notification read material is reused only during one delivery attempt. Facts, delivery plans, and projections are not long-lived caches or a second authority.
78	- A commit affecting at least eight Members queues notification effects after the durable commit and Client invalidation. Effects remain ordered per Member and are scheduled independently across Members. Effects that have not started when shutdown begins are skipped; the next activation derives the durable unread facts again.
79	- JSONL `zstd` remains the production default. Uncompressed replay is faster in the measured fixture but uses substantially more disk space.
80	- Concurrent calls already improve the measured batch Member activation path. The result alone does not justify changing Host startup ordering without a separate startup-restoration experiment.
81	- Browser cold-start results have a long tail. Keep the sample records and compare distributions; do not turn one run into a hard acceptance threshold.
82	
83	## Change workflow
84	
85	When changing a performance-sensitive path, run the narrowest scenario that can observe the change, then run the related scale cases and semantic probes. Compare the same scenario before and after the change. Inspect operation counts and result shape together with wall-clock values; a lower time with missing facts is a failed run. Run `npm test` and `npm run check:artifact` before treating the result as delivered.
86	
87	Do not place secrets, real profiles, or temporary browser overlays in the repository. The benchmark is opt-in, so ordinary development and release checks do not run it.
88

26	## Lifecycle and notifications
27	- Agent lifecycle, JSON/SQLite replay, authorization, idempotency, and revision checks stay on Host. Durable unread changes may produce one bounded coalesced Agent context notification through the public safe boundary: direct mentions carry their Message and source, Task/Claim Activities carry the complete event (actor, object, Claim refs or transfer endpoints), and ordinary unread carries only a body-free Thread-first route. Promotion is a Task activity and reaches followers through Activity markers. Notifications are not a second authority and do not promise exactly-once processing.
28	- The notice ranks missing direct signals before reminders and ordinary counts; [attention-and-messaging.md](../team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns its order, caps, and character budget.
29	- A committed Session transition (`team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-rolled-over`, `team/member-session-recycled`) records the desired binding, not a completed one: retiring the old generation and activating the target are Host effects outside the ledger write. Startup and the explicit Member recovery action both finish an interrupted transition from the recorded previous Session, and each effect derives its own completion — a live handle never proves the archive half ran. A repeated request answers with the recorded receipt and an honest status, never a second binding.
30	- Every durable Member state has one desired external effect set — the [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.md#member-lifecycle) table. Each lifecycle operation re-runs that set right after its commit, and startup re-runs it for every non-enabled Member, so an archive, suspension, or removal interrupted by a crash or a failed Workspace/Session/filesystem call converges by repeating the same derivation rather than by a second durable write.
31	- Startup never activates a non-enabled Member: an effect that fails during startup is logged and retried at the next boot instead of failing the boot. Lifecycle operations for one Member stay serialized in submission order, while different Members never queue behind each other's waits.
32	- Task reminders are Host-owned `team/reminder-raised` operations evaluated after Team events, never timers. Their optional `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta is private to one recipient; replay retains the complete episode for deduplication after its marker is consumed.
33	- Reminder operations invalidate the Task Thread change scope so the Human Inbox refreshes, but add no public fact or revision. Acceptance, close, and lifecycle cleanup remove obsolete unread markers while retaining episode history. Agent idle observations are process-local, retained across generation replacement and discarded on Host restart; unknown idle never satisfies a time condition.
34	
35	- After the ledger append, delivery effects follow — commit listeners, Client change invalidation, the participation notice, and one wake per affected Member. Each runs in a boundary that logs a failure instead of failing the operation, so a failed listener or wake still answers with the committed result, not a false rollback; only invariant divergence still rejects. A failed Inbox wake clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable Inbox facts and retries without a second append. DM keeps its explicit recorded-but-not-delivered error.
36	
37	## Which operations wake a Member, and how recovery is chosen
38	
39	A wake is one bounded coalesced notice the Host delivers over one of four causes, each carrying the durable fact that produced it:
40	
41	| Cause | What produced it |
42	| --- | --- |
43	| `commit` | any committed operation touching the Member: a mention, a DM, a Task activity, a promotion, an accepted answer |
44	| `transition` | a recorded `team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-recycled`, or legacy `team/member-session-rolled-over` whose retire and activation effects complete out of order; the rederived Inbox is sequenced after any carried input |
45	| `activation` | a fresh activation, carrying the previous Session id when input was carried forward |
46	| `running` | the Member's own `agent/status` going `running` — one wake per transition, not per step |
47	
48	Waking is not a second authority and never promises exactly-once model processing. A wake that fails delivery clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable facts and retries without a second append.
49

1	# Team 性能优化迭代
2	
3	## 问题
4	
5	Team 的性能成本分布在启动、模型 tool call 和成员协作三条链路。当前缺少一套能把用户或模型等待时间拆成 queue、ledger、通知 fan-out、Session/Agent 和 Client 阶段的统一基线，因此局部优化无法证明端到端收益。
6	
7	已有实验确认：通知路径会重复派生 Thread/Main unread 和 delivery plan，并随未读 Thread 数增长；纯读 tool 的并行分类在当前同步 projection 读取上只有很小且不稳定的收益。
8	
9	## 目标
10	
11	- 以“动作发起到结果可继续使用”的端到端 p95 为主指标。
12	- 同时记录 queue、ledger、post-commit fan-out、Session/Agent 和 Client 阶段。
13	- 保留原始 JSONL 样本、环境信息和规模输入，结果可在固定版本上复跑。
14	- 在不改变 ledger 单一权威、记录级校验、通知语义和公开协作契约的前提下，降低重复派生。
15	
16	## 选择的方案
17	
18	第一阶段按三条垂直切片推进：
19	
20	1. 建立 Team 专用 baseline runner 和默认关闭的结构化观测。
21	2. 把一次通知投递所需的 Thread/Main unread、delivery plan 和文本输入收敛成一次性只读派生结果，由 Host 在同一次投递中复用。
22	3. 用真实 Host、SQLite、Member fixture 和规模阶梯验证优化前后 p50/p95，并记录失败、冷唤醒和多 Member 场景。
23	
24	Host queue、fan-out 和协作因果使用默认关闭的结构化 hook；tool/render 阶段优先用测试 wrapper。通知 read set 只在单次投递内存在，不建立长期缓存或第二个 durable authority。
25	
26	## 关键决定
27	
28	- 主指标是端到端 p95；单个函数耗时只能作为定位信息。
29	- Thread 消息到成员回复是主协作场景；DM、Task claim 和 cold wake 作为补充场景。
30	- `team_inbox`、`team_thread read`、所有写入和所有 wake 副作用继续独占。
31	- 当前不为纯读 tool 增加 `isConcurrencySafe`。实验显示同步 projection CPU 工作无法通过 Harness parallel pool 加速，p95 收益不稳定。
32	- 跨 commit debounce、长期 read-set 缓存、通知上限调整、Member 激活并行和 Session fold 增量不进入首个实现切片。
33	- 旧版 Attention source 的升级重放与新格式稳态分别测量，不把用户未提交工作树混入 clean baseline。
34	
35	## 验收 seam
36	
37	- 启动：storage open、ledger replay/validate、Session inventory、Member activation、Host ready。
38	- Tool call：模型 call、参数处理、Host handler、queue wait、ledger/query、结果 render 和 Session 写入。
39	- 协作：A commit ack、B notice queued、B notice claimed、B read、B reply committed、B idle。
40	- 通知 read set：旧路径与新路径的 notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt、steer/followup 次序和失败隔离逐项一致。
41	- 规模：1/20/100 unread Thread、1/8/32 follower、SQLite 与内存 fixture、warm/cold Member。
42	
43	## 开放问题
44	
45	- Session fold 增量是否仍是长 Session 的主要成本，需要独立真实日志基线。
46	- Member activation 是否能安全并行，需要生命周期资源和失败边界实验。
47	- 当 Team 读取引入真实异步 I/O 后，是否重新评估纯读 tool parallel。

当前代码能通过类型检查和全量测试，先前短暂出现的 `notificationSnapshot` 缺失不再存在。但通知执行顺序和性能比较器仍有可复现问题，不能据此归档或提交为完成状态。

## Findings

### P2 — 小批次通知绕过同一 Member 已有的通知队列

**Location:** `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:2686–2692,2734–2767`；`scripts/team-performance/team-performance-semantics.ts:120–148`。

**Evidence:** 使用真实 `mountTeamMemberHost` 创建一个 Project 和 8 个 Member，连续执行两次真实 `startThread`：第一条提到全部 8 个 Member，第二条只提到其中一个。仅替换 `notifyMember` 为记录函数以观察 Host 调用次序，不改 ledger 和调度实现。第一笔提交 sequence 12 影响 9 个身份，进入延迟队列；第二笔 sequence 13 影响 2 个身份，立即执行。该 Member 的通知执行序列为 `[13, 12]`，不是 `[12, 13]`。

```text
first affected count: 9
second affected count: 2
before drain: [13]
after drain, same Member: [13, 12]
ordered: false
```

现有五项语义探针全部通过，但其中顺序探针两次都使用大批次，没有覆盖“大批次 → 小批次”。

**Impact:** 同一 Member 的提交后通知副作用不保证提交顺序。后提交的通知先执行，早提交的通知随后才重新派生当前状态；交付原因、attempt 和失败重试的执行顺序可能与提交相反。本探针证明的是调用乱序，不宣称通知正文一定倒序或 durable facts 丢失。

**Basis:** ticket 02 的“保持当前通知内容、顺序、attempt 和失败语义”；性能文档 `docs/development/team-performance.md:78` 明确承诺每个 Member 内保持顺序。

**Suggested fix:** 只要某 Member 已有待处理链，后续通知就必须进入同一链，不论新提交是否达到人数阈值。补充大→小、小→大、连续大批次及跨 Member 的顺序测试。若最终不保留延迟调度，则完整移除该路径及相应承诺，不维护两套不一致的顺序规则。

### P2 — 比较器会把测量缺失和零基线增长判为通过

**Location:** `scripts/team-performance/compare-team-performance.mjs:55–69,82–84,112–113`。

**Evidence:** 通过脚本公开 CLI，以 `--max-regression 20` 比较同一场景同一指标，实际结果如下：

| 输入 | 退出码 | 比较行数 | 回归数 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10ms → 10ms | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| 10ms → 20ms | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| 10ms → `count:0, p50/p95/p99:null` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 0ms → 20ms | 0 | 3 | 0 |

指标对象仍然存在时，空分位数只会被 `continue` 跳过，不进入缺失指标列表；零基线被转换成 `deltaPercent:null`，随后被回归过滤器排除。`count:0` 和 `null` 是 baseline 汇总器本身能生成的结构，不是无法出现的输入。

**Impact:** 评测失去原有测量，或原本测得为零的耗时变为正值时，显式回归门槛仍然返回成功。无法可靠区分“没有回归”和“已经没有有效数据”。

**Basis:** ticket 01 的比较门槛；ticket 03 的同场景性能回归验收；ticket 01:30 明确规定指定门槛时缺失指标按不兼容处理。

**Suggested fix:** 将原先可比较、现在无有效样本或无有效分位数的指标明确判为不可比较，并让门槛检查失败。单独处理零基线：零→零可通过，零→正数不得被默认为无回归。补充这些输入的 CLI 测试。

### P2 — 基准脚本没有复用 Harness 路径解析，能记录错误版本

**Location:** `scripts/team-performance/team-performance-baseline.ts:32,127–133,906`；已有实现 `scripts/harness-dir.mjs:20–29`。

**Evidence:** 使用仓库支持的相对 checkout 名 `DSH_HARNESS_DIR=deepseek-harness`：

- 公用 `harnessDir` 正确解析为 `/home/yu/projects/deepseek-harness`。
- 同样变量下运行一个 `host-boot` 样本成功，但输出 `commits.harness: "unknown"`。
- 不设置该变量的对照运行记录 Harness commit `687f282e8625c6b8d11ff58211a90524be2e4317`。

baseline 将环境变量直接交给 `git -C`，按当前 Team 目录解析；公用解析器则按 Team 的上级目录解析，并支持 `.generated-harness`。baseline 也未读取该 marker。

**Impact:** 认证 checkout 或自定义 Harness 目录下，评测结果可能缺少或错误标注实际执行的 Harness 版本，破坏固定版本复跑和结果对比的依据。

**Basis:** ticket 01 要求固定 Team/Harness 版本；`scripts/harness-dir.mjs` 是仓库明确的单一解析来源。

**Suggested fix:** 直接复用 `harnessDir`，移除 baseline 的独立路径解析；覆盖相对名称、绝对路径及 marker 场景。该问题是现成能力未复用，不需要新增依赖或配置层。

### P2 — 延迟通知的完整性错误行为与维护文档不一致

**Location:** `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts:2729–2748`；`docs/architecture/host-authority.md:35`。

**Evidence:** 当前代码已把延迟通知中的 `AgentTeamInvariantError` 提升到 `logger.error`，新增测试确认此时调用方仍得到 `committed`。但 Host 权威文档仍写“only invariant divergence still rejects”，方法注释仍称该错误在调用方栈上重新抛出。同步分支确实重抛，延迟分支则只记 error；两种行为现已不同。

**Impact:** 开发者和调用方无法从正式契约判断错误是通过调用失败还是日志报告。此次修改改变了错误传播方式，单纯提高日志级别并不等于保留原来的拒绝语义。

**Basis:** ticket 02 的失败隔离验收；`docs/AGENTS.md` 要求 Host 生命周期和通知事实归 `architecture/host-authority.md`，且文档必须如实描述实现。

**Suggested fix:** 明确采用的错误传播契约；如果保留延迟通知，正式文档、相关 package 说明和注释必须区分同步拒绝与异步 error 诊断，并说明后者不会改变已返回的提交结果。不能继续声明全部保持原语义。此项不是建议在 `setImmediate` 中无处理地抛错。

### P3 — 新性能文档缺少规定的任务导航入口

**Location:** `docs/README.md:45–51`；`docs/README.zh.md:45–51`。

**Evidence:** 两份索引表都新增了性能文档行，但对应的 “Where to start / 从哪里开始” 没有性能测量路径。自动文档检查通过，未覆盖这一维护规则。

**Impact:** 从“正在做什么”进入文档的读者无法直接找到新的测量流程。

**Basis:** `docs/AGENTS.md`：“A new maintained document gets an index row and a Where to start path in both README.md and README.zh.md in the same change.”

**Suggested fix:** 两种语言各补一条性能测量/性能改动导航，指向现有性能文档，不重复其内容。

5	## Scope
6	This document records maintenance workflows for the repository. Exact command definitions remain authoritative in the root `package.json`, package manifests, and `scripts/`; update configuration first when a command changes, then update this document.
7	
8	## Start developing
9	This repository is an independent external DSH bundle. End users install the published package; local development and real Web verification require the adjacent `../deepseek-harness` checkout.
10	
11	```text
12	../
13	├── deepseek-harness/
14	└── dsh-agent-team/
15	```
16	
17	Install dependencies with the command specified by the root README:
18	
19	```sh
20	corepack pnpm install
21	```
22	
23	`pnpm-workspace.yaml` does not declare `packages/*` as workspace members: the repository publishes one root npm package and its three `packages/*` directories are build targets of that one workspace, not independently installable packages. The file is still load-bearing — it disables automatic peer installation and carries the build-approval and release-age settings this repository relies on — so do not change or remove it because a directory lacks its own manifest. The root `node_modules` and adjacent Harness checkout provide the packages and source mappings needed for local development.
24	
25	## Verification gradient
26	Run the smallest sufficient checks for the change:
27	
28	```sh
29	npm run generate:typert
30	npm run typecheck
31	npm run check:docs
32	npm run check:core-skills
33	npm run check:boundaries
34	npm run check:versions
35	npm run check:facades
36	npm test
37	npm run build
38	npm run lint
39	npm run duplication
40	npm pack --dry-run
41	npm run check:artifact
42	npm run check:public-baseline
43	git diff --check HEAD
44	```
45	
46	Their responsibilities are:
47	
48	- `generate:typert` emits Typert Host/Remote artifacts from the Host face in `packages/agent-team/src/`.
49	- `typecheck` regenerates Typert and checks Host, tools, and Client sources.
50	- `check:docs` mechanically enforces the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md): bilingual pairing with a working switcher, a shared heading outline per pair (the same headings at the same levels), relative links, `#fragment` heading anchors, the per-file longest-block ceiling recorded in the script, and both indexes naming exactly the documents that exist. It covers the four README pairs as well — the repository root and one per package — plus the root contributing pair, each set with its own switcher wording. Run it on its own for a documentation-only change.
51	  - `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --budgets` prints the per-file longest-block table instead of deciding.
52	- `check:core-skills` mechanically enforces the shipped skill contract under `packages/agent-team/core-skills/`: the front matter names the skill after its directory and its description names real triggers, the whole skill stays inside the reviewed budget in `scripts/check-core-skills.mjs`, every relative link stays inside the skill directory (an installer copies that directory alone), and every file under `references/` is linked from `SKILL.md`.
53	- `check:boundaries` mechanically enforces the package seams described below: no file under `packages/*/src/` may reach another package by a relative specifier that escapes its own package directory. `import type` is exempt because it is erased before runtime, and test files are out of scope because they deliberately wire directories together. Declared subpaths such as `@contexera/dsh-agent-team/remote` are the supported way to cross a seam.
54	- `check:versions` mechanically enforces the certified-version consistency rule: the CI tag, the setup tag, the development guide, the READMEs, the architecture doc, the compatibility baseline, and the bug-report placeholder must all state the same DSH baseline (in both languages). That baseline must also be the lower bound of every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range. It asserts mutual agreement, never a hardcoded version, so it passes unchanged on every release lane. Run it on its own after touching any version string.
55	- `check:comments` mechanically enforces two comment rules over `packages/*/src` and `scripts/`, excluding `vendor/`. First, a per-scope comment-line budget recorded in the script (see its header). Second, a comment may not cite `.scratch/`, a work-item number, or an acceptance criterion: none of those resolve for a reader of the published package, and work history is not an authority. A bare `issue #<n>` is fine — it resolves to a real GitHub issue — and so is `Task #<n>`, a documented Team entity.
56	- `check:facades` writes nothing: it recomputes the path facades from the adjacent Harness checkout and refuses a committed `tsconfig*.json` or `.generated-harness` marker that differs from the generated output, so a subpath added to `scripts/sync-paths.mjs` cannot land without its regenerated facades. `npm test` runs it, which is why a fresh clone regenerates the facades first (see [`environments-and-install.md`](./environments-and-install.md)).
57	- `test` regenerates Typert, runs `check:facades`, `check:docs`, `check:core-skills`, `check:boundaries`, `check:versions`, and `check:comments`, then runs Vitest. `scripts/isolate-dsh-home.setup.ts` gives each test file an isolated `DSH_HOME`; tests needing a particular home must save and restore it. Startup does not prune ledger-unknown Member directories; explicit Member removal removes that Member's private memory.
58	- The suite pins one time zone (`Asia/Shanghai`, in `vitest.config.ts`), because time rendering is zone-dependent by contract: a seat states the reader's own clock, so the same expectation otherwise reads as a different hour on every runner — UTC in CI, UTC+8 where this is maintained. The pinned zone is deliberately not UTC, which keeps the assertion sharp: a formatter that reaches for `getUTCHours` renders an hour that is not the reader's and fails here. A date-sensitive test may therefore assert a literal clock time rather than read the runner's zone for its expectation.
59	- The Client bench (`packages/client-agent-team/tests/harness.tsx`) fails a spec whose rendered shipped slot entry crashed: the shipped error boundary contains the throw and reports it only through `console.error`, so an unguarded run stays green while the surface is gone. That bench also supplies what jsdom lacks (`ResizeObserver`, `document.fonts`) and the whole `conversation` service face — an absent observable member is not a missing method but a `WeakMap.set(undefined)` throw in the renderer's hook cache.
60	- `build` uses the restricted Node cleaner to clear package `lib/` directories, regenerates Typert, builds all three source trees, and uses Harness `tsdown` for the Client bundle. The published artifact remains one root npm package.
61	- `lint` runs oxlint.
62	- `duplication` runs jscpd over `packages` and `scripts` using `.jscpd.json`; treat its output as a place to look, never as a verdict, because it reports moved and restructured code as readily as copied code.
63	- `pack --dry-run` checks the root bundle's published contents; `prepack` runs the full build first, so it is a release prerequisite rather than an everyday check.
64	- `check:artifact` reads back what `npm pack` would actually ship and refuses an artifact that would ship broken: stray `.ts`/`.tsx` sources, a missing `cordis.patch.yml`, or a runtime relative import whose target is not inside the tarball. That last one is invisible to every local check, because the working tree has every file. Run it after `build` and before publishing.
65	- `check:public-baseline` compares the certified DSH baseline declared by the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers against every public surface that restates it by hand — both READMEs and the pinned compatibility discussion in the Harness repository. A surface it cannot parse is a failure, never a skip, so rewording a README cannot quietly drop it out of coverage. It needs `gh`; `--offline` skips the discussion read and is for local iteration only.
66	
67	Both gates are publish-time checks rather than everyday ones; [`release-runbook.md`](../release-runbook.md) places them in the order a release runs them.
68	
69	Changes affecting browser bundles, Client modules, slots, Remote activation, bundle manifests, or visible UI must also run:
70	
71	```sh
72	npm run test:browser
73	```
74	
75	Visible UI changes touching Team controls or surfaces additionally run the mechanical design-language audit (shipped-reference tripwires included):
76	
77	```sh
78	node scripts/audit-ui-parity.mjs
79	```
80	
81	The audit compares Team Client CSS/TSX against the design-language contract in `docs/frontend-design/principles-and-language.md`: focus visibility, control rhythm, icon semantics, hardcoded colors, and shipped-reference presence. Run it after any visible-UI change and after every DSH upgrade.
82	
83	This builds first, copies built packages into a temporary profile, starts the official Harness Web scaffold, and runs the real journey with `/usr/bin/google-chrome` (override with `CHROME_PATH`). The sandbox setup provisions Playwright's own chromium at that path when the base image ships no browser. It cleans the temporary profile and Harness test files afterward.
84	
85	There are three explicit preview/verification paths:
86	
87	```sh
88	npm run preview:ui                         # keyless Team fixture
89	npm run test:browser                       # repeatable keyless browser acceptance
90	DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... npm run preview       # real model interaction
91	```
92	
93	`preview` and `preview:ui` use temporary profiles and storage and clean up on `Ctrl+C`. `preview` always uses the real DeepSeek adapter and fails when credentials are missing; it does not silently switch to replay. `preview:ui` uses a keyless route-only adapter whose fixture does not call a model; an accidental model request fails explicitly.
94	
95	All three lanes stage this bundle and its declared dependency closure into a temporary profile, then name that staged copy as a profile package — the shape `dsh plugin add` leaves behind: a `file:` dependency, a link under the profile's own `node_modules`, and an entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The scaffold resolves plugin imports from a computed generation built out of `profile.layers`, so only a staged copy named there contributes the Team rows, and they come from the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.
96	
97	A command-line overlay is not an equivalent mount. The Host row's Human-profile form is written to the profile document, and the config editor rejects that write while a later layer (a home patch or a command-line overlay) declares the same row — `overridden by a home patch or command-line overlay` — so the form stays unwritable. A staged bundle the scaffold never names resolves neither its own rows nor its dependency closure: every Team row reports `failed to import` with no module-resolution error to read, and the keyless fixture then fails on an `undefined` `ctx.agentTeam`.
98	
99	`test:browser` does not cover the two preview lanes, so boot them by hand after any change to scaffold composition or profile resolution.
100	
101	The browser journey uses a deterministic keyless Host/Client driver. It covers Agent Inbox reading/replying, Human Project and Thread navigation, persistence after reload, and restoration of the ordinary DSH surface after leaving Team mode.
